business_problem: Gong needed a transactional, low-latency database that could keep up with tens of millions of daily customer interactions and map them to the right CRM opportunities without the slowdowns of its previous Lucene-based system.
solution_summary: Gong rebuilt the persistence layer behind its Deal Association algorithm on MongoDB Atlas so the platform could connect calls, emails, web conferences, and other engagements to the right sales opportunities in near real time. Atlas already stored transcripts, so the team expanded it into the single source of truth for customer data and relied on its ACID guarantees, sharding support, and high throughput to replace a slower non-transactional provider. Gong shards customer data across five clusters so each tenant can stay on one shard and avoid expensive cross-shard queries while still meeting SLAs. Java developers now work directly against Atlas, process associations in milliseconds, and expose faster dashboards and filters that help revenue teams act on insights before deals stall.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Gong's transcripts, customer data, and deal-association results with ACID transactions and sharding for tenant-level scale.

data_flow: Calls, emails, web conferences, text interactions, and CRM opportunity data feed Gong's Deal Association algorithm, which writes associations and customer records to MongoDB Atlas so dashboards, searches, and filters can surface revenue insights almost immediately.
business_outcome: Gong cut core processing from tens of seconds to 20-30 milliseconds, made queries ten times faster, and gave developers a scalable, easier-to-maintain foundation for its revenue intelligence platform.
